howDoI.q: How do I draw a figure that looks far away?
How do I make a far figure walk slowly?
How do I make a far figure jump smaller?
How do I make the hills paler than the figure?
How do I draw hills that go on and on?
How do I make something look farther away with big things in front?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Walking Very Far is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels about drawing someone walking a long way off, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk to the door or gate at the end of each level.

The one idea

A far figure does not need a smaller picture of everything. It needs very few pixels, the right colors, small slow steps and big things near it to measure it against. Near and Far shows a far plane drawn at half size; this game goes much further, to a figure only eight pixels tall. Maps Within Maps shows how a world, a town and a house each get their own scene and scale.

pages.head: Level 1: Up Close
pages.html:
Level 1: Up Close

Lian is his normal size here: two blocks, 40 pixels tall. The sign says so. Behind him are low hills in pale layers, and a thin road winding up them. Walk to the door on the right.

In the next level Lian walks along those hills, a very long way off.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Lian up close. The scene loads hero.chr and hero.cbl, the usual Lian: a head block over a body block, 20 pixels wide.
  • Hills that repeat. Open close.map and the Blocks tab. The hills are four layers drawn in one picture, 320 pixels wide and 120 high, cut into blocks. The picture repeats every 160 pixels (8 blocks), so the map can be as wide as you like and use the same few blocks. Each layer is paler and smoother than the one in front, and the road is drawn narrower as it climbs.
  • Distance colors. The hill layers use a ramp of five colors, dist, from a dark green-blue to nearly the sky. In this level they are only colors. In level 2 the palette changes under them.
  • A long map, a moving view. The map is 24 blocks wide and 10 high. The view starts with Lian in the middle of the screen and follows him sideways. Scrolling is on left and right and off up and down.

pages.head: Level 2: Far Away
pages.html:
Level 2: Far Away

The first scene looks the same, but Lian is a tiny figure, only 4 pixels wide and 8 tall, with a white pom-pom. The TOO FAST sign says what is wrong: he takes the same steps as up close, so he zips along like a bug and looks nearby. Walk to the gate on the right (the red flag).

The gate takes you to the same walk again, with SLOW STEPS: he moves less than half as fast and looks far away. The long path gives you time to look at the pale hills, the road and the little figure.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A tiny Lian. Open the Character tab and load quick.chr. Every frame is one block that has only a few pixels in it, standing on the bottom row, with the top block empty. Eight tiny poses are drawn by hand: standing, four walking, jumping, falling and hurt. Two scenes share tiny.cbl, the blocks.
  • Same keys, new frames. The two character files are the usual Lian with every frame swapped, so the keys and the order of the walk are the same.
  • Slow is a number. A frame says how many pixels it moves and how many ticks it lasts. quick.chr moves 4 pixels a frame, every tick, like the big Lian: about 73 pixels a second. slow.chr moves 3 pixels and waits 2 ticks: about 27 a second. Nothing slows him down while the game runs; the character file says it. His jump is smaller too: a push of 4, not 12.
  • Pale is a palette. The scenes load far.pal. It is near.pal with the sky, grass, stone, blue, purple and white ramps mixed part of the way toward pale blue. The hills, the sky and the grass are paler; Lian, the signs and the fence keep their own colors, so the figure is dark and orange on pale and stays easy to see.
  • One block, two maps. quick.map and slow.map are the same path with different signs. The scenes differ only in the character file they load.
  • Everything that stops you is drawn. The pines at each end are solid blocks. A gate is a block, and the link is on its cell.

pages.head: Level 3: Big Things in Front
pages.html:
Level 3: Big Things in Front

The same figure, the same slow walk, and the same pale hills, with a big fence and big flowers drawn along the bottom of the screen. A flower is more than six times as tall as Lian, so he must be far behind it. Two signs say how. Walk to the gate at the end.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • Size comes from neighbors. Nothing about Lian changes from level 2. The only new things are blocks in the rows under the path: a fence with wide posts and two tall flowers, drawn in strong colors that the far palette leaves alone. Next to them the pale hills and the 8 pixel Lian read as far away.
  • It repeats. The picture under the path is 160 pixels wide, so the map uses it five times with the same few blocks. Open front.map to see the fence and flowers laid in a row.
  • Lower is nearer. The big things are below the path on the screen and the hills above it, which is how a flat picture says what is close.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine’s limits, so you can plan around them.

  • No change of size while you walk. Lian does not shrink as he gets farther. A scene loads one character file, and he is that size for the whole scene. To make him smaller, load the scene with a smaller character.
  • No slow motion by itself. The engine moves him a whole number of pixels a frame. Slower is fewer pixels or a longer pause, both written in the character file.
  • No depth. The hills slide along at the same speed as the ground. A scene cannot move its far layers slower than its near ones. (The Starters named PARALLAX and BELTWAY on the Sample CD fake it another way.)
  • A tiny picture is not a tiny hero. The far Lian is eight pixels tall, but his box for bumping into things is still two blocks tall and one wide, like the near Lian’s. Keep the air above him clear.
  • Few colors. A scene has 256 colors, and the far palette makes pale ones from the same numbers. You cannot blur or fade a picture while the game runs.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Open slow.chr and change the x of the walking frames from 3 to 2, or the pause from 2 to 3. He walks even slower.
  • Load hero.chr and hero.cbl in a far scene in place of slow.chr and tiny.cbl and see the big Lian among the pale hills.
  • In the Blocks tab, edit a tiny pose: give him a different color jacket, and see if he still reads at a glance.
  • Make the haze stronger in far.pal.
  • Add a third far scene with an even smaller Lian and a thinner road.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one: Near and Far for a far plane drawn at half size, and Maps Within Maps for a world, a town and a house.
